publicCloud.ai.agents.PermissionRule.description: One tool-permission rule: which tool calls it matches, and what to do with them.

action.description: What to do with a matching call.

args.description: Argument constraints, as 'path-glob -> value-glob', ALL of which must hold for the rule to match. The call's arguments are flattened to 'path -> value' pairs before matching ('{'a':{'b':[1,2]}}' becomes 'a.b.0 -> 1', 'a.b.1 -> 2'), so one entry means 'some argument whose path matches the key has a value matching the pattern'. A '!' prefix on the value inverts it into '… and none of them matches', which is how an allowlist is written: '{'url': '!https://*.ovh.net/*'}' is every URL but ours. '!' flips the value test and not the quantifier: both forms ask whether SOME selected value satisfies the test. So a deny rule reading '{'url': '!https://*.ovh.net/*'}' still fires on a call carrying two URLs of which only one is foreign — which is the point of it. A rule about an argument that is absent entirely never matches, in either form: absence is not a value to have an opinion about, and a rule that fired on it would fire on every unrelated call.

phase.description: Whether this rule is evaluated before the call runs or after it returned. Defaults to 'before'.

reason.description: Why this rule exists. Shown to the model in the refusal and written to the log. Worth filling in: it is the only part of this rule the model can act on.

result.description: Value-glob over the text the tool returned. 'phase: after' only. Matched against the raw result, not flattened into paths the way 'args' is: a result is prose far more often than it is a shape, and an author writing a rule about one should not have to know whether this particular tool happened to wrap it in JSON. '*' spans everything, so ''*-----BEGIN * PRIVATE KEY*'' is a substring test, and a leading '!' inverts it exactly as it does in 'args'. A rule with no 'result' matches every result, which is how 'refer everything this tool brings back to the judge' is written.

tool.description: Glob over the tool name. '*' matches any run of characters, including an empty one, so a rule left at its default matches every tool.

triggers.description: Trigger kinds this rule applies to ('http', 'invoke', 'messaging', 'cron', 'scheduled', 'subagent'). Empty means every trigger.

unattended.description: What an 'ask' becomes on a turn with no human to ask. Defaults to 'deny'; ignored unless 'action' is 'ask'.

publicCloud.ai.agents.PermissionRulePhas.description: Whether this rule is evaluated before the call runs or after it returned. Defaults to 'before'.

It decides which flavors can boot the image, and Windows images carry a license. `LINUX`: A Linux (or other non-Windows) image for virtual instances. `WINDOWS`: A Microsoft Windows image. It can only boot on Windows flavors. `BAREMETAL_LINUX`: A Linux image for bare-metal instances.

publicCloud.instance.ImageStatusEnum.description: Lifecycle status of an instance image as reported by OpenStack Glance. It describes where the image is in its upload and availability lifecycle. `QUEUED`: The image identifier has been reserved in the image registry, but no image data has been uploaded yet. `SAVING`: The raw image data is currently being uploaded to the image store. `IMPORTING`: The uploaded image data is being imported and processed through the Glance import workflow. `ACTIVE`: The image is fully available and can be used to boot instances. `DEACTIVATED`: Access to the image has been disabled by an administrator. The data is preserved but the image cannot be used to launch instances until reactivated. `KILLED`: An error occurred during upload or import and the image data is not usable. `PENDING_DELETE`: The image has been marked for deletion but its data has not been removed yet. It may still be restorable during the retention delay. `DELETED`: The image has been deleted and its data is scheduled for removal.

publicCloud.instance.ImageVisibilityEnum.description: Image visibility. Controls which projects can see and use an instance image, as defined by OpenStack Glance. `PUBLIC`: The image is visible to and usable by every project. `PRIVATE`: The image is visible only to the project that owns it. `SHARED`: The image is visible only to the owning project and the specific projects it has been explicitly shared with (image members). `COMMUNITY`: The image is usable by every project but is hidden from default image listings, so it must be requested explicitly.

publicCloud.instance.Instance.description: A Public Cloud compute instance: a virtual machine provisioned from a flavor and an image, connected to one or more networks and backed by block volumes. The resource follows the standard desired-state / observed-state model: targetSpec holds the specification you asked for. currentState reflects what the compute backend actually reports. resourceStatus and currentTasks describe the reconciliation between the two. Updates are performed by sending a new targetSpec on the PUT route. The requested operations (rename, resize, power change, volume attach/detach, share attach/detach) are derived from the diff.

checksum.description: Computed hash representing the current targetSpec value. It enables optional optimistic concurrency control: the value returned by a GET may be sent back in the PUT and action payloads, and the request is then rejected with a 409 checksum-mismatch conflict if it no longer matches server-side (because another request modified the instance in the meantime). Sending no checksum skips that check and forces the write (last-write-wins).

createdAt.description: Creation date of the instance, as an ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp

currentState.description: Current observed state of the instance as reported by the compute backend (name, flavor, image, location, power state, networks, attached volumes, attached shares, security groups). It is null while the instance is still being created and no backend state is available yet.

currentTasks.description: In-progress operations. Ongoing asynchronous tasks reconciling currentState toward targetSpec, for example a create, resize, reboot, volume attach or share attach. Poll the instance until this list is empty and resourceStatus is READY to know the requested change has been applied.

id.description: Unique identifier of the instance

resourceStatus.description: Resource lifecycle status. High-level readiness of the instance in the system, for example CREATING, READY, UPDATING, DELETING, ERROR. This is distinct from currentState.powerState, which carries the lower-level OpenStack administrative power state of the virtual machine.

targetSpec.description: Desired specification. Last target specification requested for the instance. On update, the difference between the previous and the new targetSpec determines the operations performed (rename, resize, power change, and declarative volume/share attach-detach).

updatedAt.description: Last modification date of the instance, as an ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp

publicCloud.instance.InstanceActionParam.description: Optional parameters refining an imperative instance action. Each field applies only to a specific action type (see InstanceActionTypeEnum) and is ignored for other actions.

hard.description: Applies only to the REBOOT action. When true, performs a hard reboot (power cycle) instead of a graceful, soft reboot. Defaults to a soft reboot.

imageId.description: Applies only to the RESCUE action. Identifier of the image to boot the instance from while in rescue mode. When omitted, the backend selects a default rescue image.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceActionReque.description: Instance action request. Payload for triggering an imperative action on an instance, for example lock, reboot or rescue. Unlike the declarative PUT update, an action directly commands an administrative or operational state change. The checksum from the last GET may be supplied to opt in to optimistic concurrency control. Omitting it forces the action.

checksum.description: Concurrency-control checksum. Optional checksum obtained from the last GET of the instance. When supplied, it must still match the instance's current checksum or the action is rejected with a 409 checksum-mismatch conflict, protecting against a concurrent modification. When omitted or empty, the concurrency check is skipped and the action is forced (last-write-wins).

parameters.description: Optional parameters refining the requested action (see InstanceActionParameters). Only relevant for actions that accept options, such as a hard REBOOT or a RESCUE with a specific image. Omit for actions that take none.

type.description: Action type. The imperative action to perform on the instance (see InstanceActionTypeEnum: LOCK, UNLOCK, REBOOT, RESCUE, UNRESCUE, STOP, START, SHELVE, UNSHELVE, PAUSE, UNPAUSE, SUSPEND, RESUME).

publicCloud.instance.InstanceActionTypeE.description: Instance action type. Imperative action that can be triggered on an instance to change its administrative or operational state. `LOCK`: Lock the instance to prevent further actions on it, protecting it from accidental or unauthorized operations. `UNLOCK`: Remove a previously set lock, re-enabling actions on the instance. `REBOOT`: Restart the instance. `RESCUE`: Boot the instance into rescue mode from a rescue image so its root disk can be inspected or repaired. `UNRESCUE`: Return the instance from rescue mode to normal operation. `STOP`: Power off the instance. Its resources remain allocated. `START`: Power on a stopped instance. `SHELVE`: Power off the instance and release its compute resources so it can be resumed later. `UNSHELVE`: Resume a shelved instance. `PAUSE`: Freeze a running instance, keeping its memory state in the RAM of the host. `UNPAUSE`: Return a paused instance to normal operation. `SUSPEND`: Save the memory state of a running instance to disk and stop it. Its resources remain allocated. `RESUME`: Restore a suspended instance from its saved memory state.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceAvailableAc.description: Instance action availability. One instance action type and whether it can currently be triggered on the instance through the action endpoint.

available.description: Whether the action can currently be triggered through the action endpoint. A call with an unavailable action is refused.

name.description: Action type, as accepted by the action endpoint

publicCloud.instance.InstanceCreation.description: Instance creation payload. Request body for creating a Public Cloud instance (POST). It wraps the desired InstanceTargetSpec, which carries every settable field including those that become immutable once the instance exists (location, sshKeyName, placement group). userData (cloud-init) is write-only — never echoed back on GET/LIST — and, unlike those fields, remains mutable after creation via PUT, though any change to it reinstalls the instance.

targetSpec.description: Desired specification. Full target specification of the instance to create. See InstanceTargetSpec for the per-field creation rules and immutability constraints.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceCurrentStat.description: Current observed state of the instance as reported by the compute backend (OpenStack/Nova). It is read-only and reflects what actually exists, as opposed to targetSpec which holds what was requested. Some collections (notably shares) are only populated on a GET of a single instance and are omitted from the LIST response.

availableActions.description: Availability of every instance action type given the current state of the instance. Always contains exactly one entry per InstanceActionTypeEnum value, in the order of that enum, each flagged with whether it can currently be triggered through the action endpoint. For example, when the instance is locked only UNLOCK is available. While a task is in progress on the instance or when it is in error, none is available.

flavor.description: Observed flavor of the instance with full details (name, vCPUs, RAM, local disk). See InstanceFlavor.

group.description: Reference to the instance (placement) group the instance belongs to. Null when it is not part of any group. Immutable after creation.

hostId.description: Opaque identifier of the physical host the instance is running on, as exposed by OpenStack. Null when not available.

image.description: Observed image the instance was booted from, with full details (name, size, status). Null for boot-from-volume instances, which have no image. See InstanceImage.

location.description: Location. Observed region and availability zone where the instance is provisioned. See InstanceLocation.

locked.description: Lock state. Whether the instance is locked against modifications. When locked, mutating actions are refused until it is unlocked (see the LOCK/UNLOCK actions in InstanceActionTypeEnum).

name.description: Observed display name of the instance

networks.description: Observed network interfaces of the instance, with full details (network, subnet, gateway and per-interface addresses). One entry per network, plus at most one entry without an id for the public (Ext-Net) interface. Every address of the instance is reported through the entry's addresses list, each address typed FIXED, FLOATING or ADDITIONAL. There is no separate scalar address field. See InstanceNetwork.

powerState.description: Actual administrative power state of the instance as reported by OpenStack (see PowerStateEnum). This may transiently differ from targetSpec.powerState while a power transition is in progress.

projectId.description: Identifier of the Public Cloud project the instance belongs to

securityGroups.description: References to the security groups currently attached to the instance's ports

shares.description: Observed instance-side share attachments. Only populated on a GET of a single instance (never in list responses). Mixing per-share access rules (managed directly on the share resource) with instance-side attach on the same share is unsupported and will show the share OUT_OF_SYNC. See InstanceShare.

sshKeyName.description: Name of the SSH key pair injected into the instance at boot. Null when none was provided.

userId.description: Identifier of the OpenStack user that owns the instance

volumes.description: Observed block volumes attached to the instance, with details (name, size). See InstanceVolume.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceFlavor.description: Observed flavor of an instance, carrying the full sizing details as reported by the backend. Used in currentState. The creation/update side references a flavor by id through InstanceFlavorRef.

bandwidth.description: Network bandwidth of the flavor in Mbit/s. Null when the flavor is not in the catalog.

disk.description: Size of the flavor's local root disk in GB

gpus.description: Number of physical GPUs provided by the flavor, 0 for flavors without GPU

id.description: Unique identifier of the flavor

name.description: Human-readable flavor name, for example the commercial flavor label

ram.description: Amount of RAM provided by the flavor in MB

vcpus.description: Number of virtual CPUs provided by the flavor

publicCloud.instance.InstanceFlavorRef.description: User-controlled reference to the flavor that sizes the instance, used in targetSpec. It carries only the flavor id. The full observed sizing is exposed in currentState through InstanceFlavor.

id.description: Identifier of the flavor to size the instance with. Changing it on update triggers a resize.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceGroupRef.description: Reference to the instance (placement) group the instance belongs to, controlling affinity/anti-affinity placement. Used in targetSpec to place the instance at creation and echoed in currentState. The group is set only at creation time and is immutable afterward. OpenStack/Nova server groups cannot be changed, so membership cannot be modified on a running instance.

id.description: Identifier of the instance group. Honored only at creation time. The group cannot be changed afterward.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceImage.description: Observed image an instance was booted from, carrying the full details as reported by OpenStack Glance. Used in currentState. The creation/update side references an image by id through InstanceImageRef.

defaultUser.description: Default login user of the image, as set by its publisher, for example almalinux or ubuntu. Null when the image declares none.

deprecated.description: Whether the image is flagged as deprecated. A deprecated image can still boot existing instances but is no longer recommended for new ones.

id.description: Unique identifier of the image

name.description: Human-readable image name. Null when not reported by the backend.

size.description: Size of the image in bytes. Null when the backend does not report it.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the image as reported by Glance (see ImageStatusEnum). Null when not reported.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceImageRef.description: User-controlled reference to the image the instance boots from, used in targetSpec. It carries only the image id. The full observed image is exposed in currentState through InstanceImage.

id.description: Identifier of the image to boot from. Changing it on update triggers a rebuild of the instance.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceLocation.description: Instance location. Geographic placement of an instance: the region and, optionally, the availability zone within that region. In targetSpec it is the desired placement (immutable after creation). In currentState it is the observed placement.

availabilityZone.description: Availability zone within the region where the instance is placed. When omitted at creation the backend selects a zone automatically. Immutable after creation.

region.description: Code of the region where the instance is provisioned, for example GRA11, BHS5. Immutable after creation. An instance cannot be moved to another region.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceNetwork.description: Observed network interface attached to an instance, with full details as reported by the backend. Used in currentState. The creation/update side declares interfaces through InstanceNetworkRef.

addresses.description: Every IP address through which the instance is reachable on this interface, each with its type, IP version and MAC address. It carries the interface's fixed addresses and, where applicable, the floating IP associated with it and any additional IPs routed to it. This is the single source of truth for the instance's observed addresses. Null or empty only while no address has been assigned yet. See InstanceNetworkAddress.

gatewayId.description: Identifier of the gateway providing egress for this interface. Null when none applies.

id.description: Identifier of the network this interface is attached to, or null for the public (Ext-Net) interface. There is at most one entry without an id: additional IPs are reported as ADDITIONAL addresses of that public entry instead of forming their own entry.

subnetId.description: Identifier of the subnet this interface draws its fixed address from, or null for an entry without a network id

publicCloud.instance.InstanceNetworkAddr.description: A single IP address bound to an instance network interface, with its associated MAC address, IP version and address type

ip.description: IP address assigned to the interface (IPv4 or IPv6)

mac.description: MAC address of the interface this IP is bound to. Null when the backend reports no interface for the address, which happens for an additional IP routed to an instance whose public interface has no visible Ext-Net address yet.

type.description: Address type. How this address reaches the instance: FIXED for an address assigned to the interface itself, FLOATING for a floating IP NAT'd onto it, ADDITIONAL for an additional IP routed to the public interface. See InstanceNetworkAddressTypeEnum.

version.description: IP version of the address (4 for IPv4, 6 for IPv6)

publicCloud.instance.InstanceNetworkAddr.description: Instance network address type. Nature of an IP address observed on an instance network interface, telling how the address reaches the instance. `FIXED`: An address assigned to the interface itself: the fixed address of a private interface (whether assigned by IPAM or pinned), or the platform-assigned or pinned Ext-Net address of the public interface. `FLOATING`: A floating IP NAT'd onto this interface: the address is not configured on the interface, the network translates it to the interface's fixed address. `ADDITIONAL`: An additional IP (also known as a failover IP, implemented as an ipalias) routed to the instance's public interface.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceNetworkRef.description: Instance network reference (desired). User-controlled entry declaring one network interface to attach to the instance in targetSpec. Which fields are set determines the meaning of the entry: * autoAssignPublicIp alone. A public (Ext-Net) interface with a platform-assigned public IP. At most one entry of the list may set it. * ip alone, without an id and without a subnetId. A public IP the project already owns: either an additional IP, or an Ext-Net IP of the project in the instance's region. Any other address is rejected. Such an entry implicitly attaches the public (Ext-Net) interface. Several of them are allowed, and they may coexist with an autoAssignPublicIp entry. * subnetId, with an optional id. A private interface whose fixed address is assigned by IPAM. * subnetId and ip, with an optional id. A private interface where ip pins the fixed address when it falls inside the subnet CIDR, and otherwise designates an EXISTING floating IP to associate with that interface. When id is omitted on a private interface, the network of subnetId is used. When id is given, subnetId must belong to it. The enclosing networks list is declarative: adding or removing an entry attaches or detaches the corresponding interface on update.

autoAssignPublicIp.description: Auto-assign public IP. Whether to attach a public (Ext-Net) interface with a public IP assigned by the platform. Only allowed on an entry that has no id, no subnetId and no ip, and at most one entry of the networks list may set it. Requires the optional instance/usePublicIP IAM action.

id.description: Identifier of the private network to attach to. Optional on a private interface: when omitted, the network of subnetId is used. Omit it on an entry declaring public connectivity through autoAssignPublicIp or ip.

ip.description: Address of this interface, whose meaning depends on the sibling fields. Without an id and a subnetId: a public IP the project already owns. An additional IP, or an Ext-Net IP of the project in the instance's region. Any other address is rejected, and the entry implicitly attaches the public (Ext-Net) interface. On a private entry (subnetId, with an optional id): pins the interface's fixed address when the address falls inside the subnet CIDR, and otherwise designates an EXISTING floating IP to associate with that interface. A public address requires the optional instance/usePublicIP IAM action.

subnetId.description: Identifier of the subnet the interface draws its fixed address from. Required for a private interface. Leave unset on an entry declaring public connectivity.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceReadTargetS.description: Desired instance specification as returned on read. Last target specification requested for the instance, as returned on read (GET/LIST). It mirrors InstanceTargetSpec but relaxes the create-only constraints: fields that are mandatory at creation are not required here, and image is nullable because boot-from-volume instances have no image.

flavor.description: Reference to the flavor that sizes the instance (vCPUs, RAM, local disk). Carries only the flavor id. Changing the referenced flavor on PUT triggers a resize of the instance.

group.description: Optional reference to the instance (placement) group the instance is created into, controlling affinity/anti-affinity placement. Immutable: the group is set only at creation time. OpenStack/Nova server groups are immutable. There is no group change on PUT and membership cannot be changed after the instance exists.

image.description: Reference to the image the instance boots from. Carries only the image id. Changing the referenced image on PUT triggers a rebuild of the instance from the new image. Null for boot-from-volume instances, which have no backing image.

location.description: Target location. Region (and optional availability zone) where the instance is provisioned. Immutable after creation. An instance cannot be moved to another region/zone, which is why location is absent from InstanceUpdateTargetSpec.

name.description: Desired display name of the instance. Changing it on PUT triggers a rename.

networks.description: Declarative list of network interfaces the instance is attached to. An entry with a subnetId, and an optional id, is a private interface, optionally carrying an ip to pin its fixed address or to associate an existing floating IP. An entry with autoAssignPublicIp alone requests a public (Ext-Net) interface with a platform-assigned public IP. An entry with ip alone attaches a public IP the project already owns, either an additional IP or an Ext-Net IP of the project in the instance's region. See InstanceNetworkRef. The list drives the desired network topology: adding or removing an entry attaches or detaches the corresponding interface on update.

powerState.description: Desired administrative power state of the instance (see PowerStateEnum: ACTIVE, PAUSED, RESCUE, SHELVED, SHUTOFF, SUSPENDED). Changing it on PUT drives the corresponding power transition (start, stop, shelve, rescue, pause, suspend). Defaults to ACTIVE.

securityGroups.description: Optional list of references to the security groups applied to all of the instance's ports. Each entry carries the security group id. Changing this list on PUT re-applies the resulting set of security groups to every instance port.

shares.description: Declarative list of file storage (shares) attached to the instance, managed exactly like volumes: the diff of this list on PUT drives attach/detach. Attaching a share creates a Manila IP access rule for the instance's interface on the share's network. The instance must have an interface on that network or the operation errors. Detaching (removing an entry from this list) deletes the matching access rule and is idempotent. Each entry's accessLevel defaults to READ_WRITE when omitted (see InstanceShareRef).

sshKeyName.description: Name of the SSH key pair injected into the instance at boot for initial access. Immutable / create-only: the key is injected once during provisioning and cannot be changed afterward, which is why sshKeyName is absent from InstanceUpdateTargetSpec.

volumes.description: Declarative list of block volumes attached to the instance, each referencing a volume by id (see InstanceVolumeRef). Attach/detach is driven by diffing this list on PUT. There is no imperative attach/detach sub-route. Adding a volume reference attaches that volume. Removing one detaches it.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceShare.description: Observed instance-side share attachment, describing the Manila IP access rule that grants the instance access to a file storage (share). This list is only populated on a GET of a single instance. It is never returned in the LIST response. Mixing per-share access rules managed directly on the share resource with instance-side attach on the SAME share is unsupported and will make the share report OUT_OF_SYNC.

accessLevel.description: Observed access level of the access rule for this instance (see FileStorageAccessLevelEnum: READ_ONLY, READ_WRITE)

accessTo.description: The instance IP address the Manila access rule targets. The instance's fixed IPv4 address on the share's network.

id.description: Identifier of the attached file storage (share)

state.description: Observed state of the underlying access rule (see FileStorageAccessRuleStateEnum: ACTIVE, APPLYING, DENYING, ERROR). Null while no state has been reported yet.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceShareRef.description: User-controlled reference declaring a file storage (share) to attach to the instance, used within the declarative shares list of targetSpec. It carries the share id and the desired access level for the attachment. Attaching creates a Manila IP access rule for the instance's interface on the share's network. The enclosing shares list is diffed on update to drive attach/detach, exactly like volumes.

accessLevel.description: Desired access level granted to the instance for this share (see FileStorageAccessLevelEnum: READ_ONLY, READ_WRITE). Defaults to READ_WRITE.

id.description: Identifier of the file storage (share) to attach. Adding this reference attaches the share to the instance. Removing it from the shares list detaches it.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceTargetSpec.description: Desired instance specification (creation). User-controlled specification of a compute instance, as supplied on creation (POST). It carries every settable field, including fields that become immutable once the instance exists (location, sshKeyName, group). Networks, volumes and shares are declarative lists: on update, the requested topology is reconciled by diffing these lists against the current attachments. The PUT route uses a reduced InstanceUpdateTargetSpec that only exposes the mutable fields.

flavor.description: Reference to the flavor that sizes the instance (vCPUs, RAM, local disk). Carries only the flavor id. Changing the referenced flavor on PUT triggers a resize of the instance.

group.description: Optional reference to the instance (placement) group the instance is created into, controlling affinity/anti-affinity placement. Immutable after creation. The group is set only at creation time. OpenStack/Nova server groups are immutable. There is no group change on PUT and membership cannot be changed after the instance exists.

image.description: Reference to the image the instance boots from. Carries only the image id. Changing the referenced image on PUT triggers a rebuild of the instance from the new image.

location.description: Target location. Region (and optional availability zone) where the instance is provisioned. Immutable after creation. An instance cannot be moved to another region/zone, which is why location is absent from InstanceUpdateTargetSpec.

name.description: Desired display name of the instance. Changing it on PUT triggers a rename.

networks.description: Declarative list of network interfaces the instance is attached to. An entry with a subnetId, and an optional id, is a private interface, optionally carrying an ip to pin its fixed address or to associate an existing floating IP. An entry with autoAssignPublicIp alone requests a public (Ext-Net) interface with a platform-assigned public IP. An entry with ip alone attaches a public IP the project already owns, either an additional IP or an Ext-Net IP of the project in the instance's region. See InstanceNetworkRef. The list drives the desired network topology: adding or removing an entry attaches or detaches the corresponding interface on update.

powerState.description: Desired administrative power state of the instance (see PowerStateEnum: ACTIVE, PAUSED, RESCUE, SHELVED, SHUTOFF, SUSPENDED). Changing it on PUT drives the corresponding power transition (start, stop, shelve, rescue, pause, suspend). Defaults to ACTIVE.

securityGroups.description: Optional list of references to the security groups applied to all of the instance's ports. Each entry carries the security group id. Changing this list on PUT re-applies the resulting set of security groups to every instance port.

shares.description: Declarative list of file storage (shares) attached to the instance, managed exactly like volumes: the diff of this list on PUT drives attach/detach. Attaching a share creates a Manila IP access rule for the instance's interface on the share's network. The instance must have an interface on that network or the operation errors. Detaching (removing an entry from this list) deletes the matching access rule and is idempotent. Each entry's accessLevel defaults to READ_WRITE when omitted (see InstanceShareRef).

sshKeyName.description: Name of the SSH key pair injected into the instance at boot for initial access. Immutable after creation. The key is injected once during provisioning and cannot be changed afterward, which is why sshKeyName is absent from InstanceUpdateTargetSpec.

userData.description: User data (cloud-init). Base64-encoded (strict standard encoding) cloud-init payload handed to the instance at boot through the OpenStack metadata service / config drive, and interpreted by cloud-init inside the guest image. The submitted string itself must be at most 65535 bytes once base64-encoded. Write-only: never returned by GET/LIST. Deliberately absent from InstanceReadTargetSpec and InstanceCurrentState. Not persisted or stored by the Public Cloud API: the payload is handed to the compute service, which makes it available to the instance via the metadata service. Only a non-reversible fingerprint of the value is retained, for change detection. Mutable, but destructively: changing userData on PUT REINSTALLS the instance (a Nova rebuild on the current image), wiping the root disk and all data on it. See InstanceUpdateTargetSpec for the tri-state update semantics.

volumes.description: Declarative list of block volumes attached to the instance, each referencing a volume by id (see InstanceVolumeRef). Attach/detach is driven by diffing this list on PUT. There is no imperative attach/detach sub-route. Adding a volume reference attaches that volume. Removing one detaches it.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceUpdate.description: Instance update payload. Request body for updating a Public Cloud instance (PUT). It wraps the reduced InstanceUpdateTargetSpec (mutable fields only) together with an optional checksum for optimistic concurrency control. The operation actually performed (rename, resize, power change, volume/share attach-detach) is derived from the diff against the current targetSpec.

checksum.description: Concurrency-control checksum. Optional checksum obtained from the last GET of the instance. When supplied, it must still match the instance's current checksum or the update is rejected with a 409 checksum-mismatch conflict, protecting against a concurrent modification. When omitted or empty, the concurrency check is skipped and the update is forced (last-write-wins).

targetSpec.description: Desired specification (mutable fields). Updated target specification restricted to the fields that can change after creation. Immutable fields (location, sshKeyName, placement group) are intentionally absent. See InstanceUpdateTargetSpec. userData is write-only (never echoed back) and follows tri-state semantics. Changing it (clearing or replacing) reinstalls the instance.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceUpdateTarge.description: Desired instance specification (update). Reduced target specification used on the PUT route, exposing only the fields that can change after creation. Immutable, create-only fields are intentionally absent: location, sshKeyName and the placement group cannot be changed once the instance exists. Networks, volumes and shares remain declarative: the requested topology is reconciled by diffing these lists against the current attachments.

flavor.description: Reference to the desired flavor (vCPUs, RAM, local disk). Carries only the flavor id. Sending a different flavor triggers a resize of the instance.

image.description: Reference to the desired image. Carries only the image id. Sending a different image triggers a rebuild of the instance from the new image.

name.description: Desired display name of the instance. Changing it triggers a rename.

networks.description: Declarative list of network interfaces the instance is attached to (see InstanceNetworkRef). The list drives the desired network topology: adding or removing an entry attaches or detaches the corresponding interface.

powerState.description: Desired administrative power state (see PowerStateEnum: ACTIVE, PAUSED, RESCUE, SHELVED, SHUTOFF, SUSPENDED). Changing it drives the corresponding power transition (start, stop, shelve, rescue, pause, suspend). A move OpenStack cannot make in one step, such as PAUSED to SHUTOFF, is rejected with ResourceInInvalidState before anything changes. The error message gives the route through ACTIVE. Defaults to ACTIVE.

securityGroups.description: Optional list of references to the security groups applied to all of the instance's ports. Changing this list re-applies the resulting set of security groups to every instance port.

shares.description: Declarative list of file storage (shares) attached to the instance, managed exactly like volumes: the diff of this list drives attach/detach. Attaching a share creates a Manila IP access rule for the instance's interface on the share's network. The instance must have an interface on that network or the operation errors. Detaching (removing an entry from this list) deletes the matching access rule and is idempotent. Each entry's accessLevel defaults to READ_WRITE when omitted (see InstanceShareRef).

userData.description: User data (cloud-init). Base64-encoded (strict standard encoding) cloud-init payload, at most 65535 bytes once base64-encoded. Write-only: never returned by GET/LIST. Not persisted or stored by the Public Cloud API: the payload is handed to the compute service, which makes it available to the instance via the metadata service on boot/rebuild. Only a non-reversible fingerprint of the value is retained, for change detection. Tri-state: omitted or null keeps the current value unchanged. An empty string clears it. A non-empty value replaces it. Destructive: any change (clear or replace) REINSTALLS the instance — a Nova rebuild on the current image — wiping the root disk and all data on it.

volumes.description: Declarative list of block volumes attached to the instance (see InstanceVolumeRef). Attach/detach is driven by diffing this list. Adding a reference attaches the volume, removing one detaches it. There is no imperative attach/detach sub-route.

publicCloud.instance.InstanceVolume.description: Observed block volume attached to an instance, carrying the details reported by the backend. Used in currentState. The creation/update side references a volume by id through InstanceVolumeRef.

publicCloud.instance.PowerStateEnum.description: Power state of an instance as reported by OpenStack Nova, also used to express the desired power state when driving the instance. `ACTIVE`: The instance is running and powered on. `PAUSED`: The instance is paused: its state is frozen in the memory of the host, which keeps its resources allocated. `SHUTOFF`: The instance is powered off (stopped) but its resources remain allocated. `SHELVED`: The instance is shelved: it is powered off and its compute resources are released, so it can be unshelved later to resume it. `SUSPENDED`: The instance is suspended: its memory state is saved to disk and it stops running, but its resources remain allocated. `RESCUE`: The instance is booted in rescue mode from a rescue image.

publicCloud.instance.RemoteConsoleProtoc.description: Underlying protocol used to reach an instance's remote console. `VNC`: VNC remote framebuffer protocol, giving graphical access to the instance console. `SPICE`: SPICE remote display protocol, offering richer graphical console access. `SERIAL`: Serial console protocol, giving text-based access to the instance's serial port.

publicCloud.instance.RemoteConsoleTypeEn.description: Concrete console client/endpoint type returned when requesting access to an instance's remote console, combining a display technology with its transport. `NOVNC`: Browser-based VNC client (noVNC) served over the VNC protocol. `XVPVNC`: Xen VNC Proxy (xvpvnc) console, accessed with a dedicated VNC client. `SPICE_HTML5`: Browser-based SPICE client (spice-html5) served over the SPICE protocol. `SERIAL`: Serial console exposed over a websocket connection.

publicCloud.instanceGroup.InstanceGroup.description: Instance group (placement group). A Public Cloud instance group, backed by an OpenStack/Nova server group, that constrains how its member instances are placed relative to one another (see policy and PolicyEnum: AFFINITY / ANTI_AFFINITY). An instance group is immutable once created: there is no update (PUT) route, and its membership is fixed. Instances join a group only at instance-creation time, through the instance's targetSpec.group field. They cannot be added to or removed from a group afterward. The only lifecycle operations are create (POST), read (GET/LIST) and delete (DELETE). The object follows the standard envelope: targetSpec is the desired specification supplied on creation, while currentState reflects what the backend actually reports (including the current members).

checksum.description: Checksum. Computed hash of the current target specification, used for optimistic concurrency control. Because an instance group has no update route, this value never changes after creation.

createdAt.description: Creation date. Timestamp at which the instance group was created, in RFC 3339 format.

currentState.description: Actual state of the instance group as reported by the backend (OpenStack/Nova server group), including its current members. This is read-only and reflects reality, in contrast to targetSpec which is the desired specification supplied on creation. May be null while the group is still being provisioned and no backend state is known yet.

currentTasks.description: Current tasks. Asynchronous operations currently running against this instance group, for example the initial provisioning or the deletion. Empty or null when no operation is in progress.

id.description: Unique identifier of the instance group, assigned at creation and used to reference it on the GET/DELETE routes

resourceStatus.description: Lifecycle status of the instance group in the system, for example whether it is being created, ready, or being deleted. Reflects readiness of the resource, not the placement policy itself.

targetSpec.description: Target specification. Desired specification of the instance group as supplied on creation (name, location and placement policy). Since an instance group cannot be updated, this specification is fixed for the lifetime of the group. Compare it against currentState to see what the backend actually provisioned.

publicCloud.instanceGroup.InstanceGroupC.description: Instance group creation payload. Request body for creating a Public Cloud instance group (POST). It wraps the desired InstanceGroupTargetSpec. Creation is the only way to define a group's placement policy: the group is immutable afterward (no PUT route), and instances join it exclusively at instance-creation time via the instance's targetSpec.group field.

targetSpec.description: Target specification. Desired specification of the instance group to create: its name, location and placement policy (see PolicyEnum). All of these values are fixed for the lifetime of the group, as instance groups cannot be updated once created.

publicCloud.instanceGroup.InstanceGroupC.description: Actual state of an instance group as reported by the backend (OpenStack/Nova server group). This is read-only: it reflects what the backend observes, in contrast to the desired InstanceGroupTargetSpec supplied on creation. Besides the group's name, location and placement policy, it exposes the current membership. Membership is fixed once instances are created: instances join a group only at instance-creation time via the instance's targetSpec.group field, and there is no route to add or remove members afterward.

location.description: Location. Region (and, where applicable, availability zone) where the instance group and its member instances are deployed, as observed on the backend.

members.description: Instances currently belonging to this group, each referenced by its identifier (see InstanceGroupMemberRef). Membership is determined at instance-creation time via the instance's targetSpec.group field and cannot be changed afterward. Null or empty when the group has no member instances.

name.description: Display name of the instance group as reported by the backend. Fixed for the lifetime of the group, since instance groups cannot be updated.

policy.description: Placement policy currently enforced for the group's members (see PolicyEnum): AFFINITY packs members onto the same hypervisor, ANTI_AFFINITY spreads them across distinct hypervisors. Mirrors the underlying OpenStack/Nova server group policy and is fixed at creation.

publicCloud.instanceGroup.InstanceGroupM.description: Reference to a single instance that is a member of an instance group. It appears in the group's currentState.members list and identifies the member by its instance id. Membership is established at instance-creation time via the instance's targetSpec.group field and is immutable: an instance cannot be added to or removed from a group afterward.

id.description: Unique identifier of the instance that belongs to the group. Use it to look up the full instance on the compute instance route.

publicCloud.instanceGroup.InstanceGroupT.description: Desired instance group specification (creation). User-controlled specification of an instance group, as supplied on creation (POST). It carries every settable field: name, location and placement policy. All of these fields are immutable once the group exists. An instance group has no update (PUT) route, so this specification is fixed for the lifetime of the group. Membership is not part of this spec: instances join the group only at instance-creation time via the instance's targetSpec.group field.

location.description: Target location. Region (and optional availability zone) where the instance group, and therefore its member instances, are placed. Immutable after creation. A group cannot be moved to another region/zone, and its members must be created in this same location.

name.description: Desired display name of the instance group. Immutable after creation, as instance groups cannot be updated.

policy.description: Placement policy applied to the group's member instances (see PolicyEnum): AFFINITY packs members onto the same hypervisor, while ANTI_AFFINITY spreads members across distinct hypervisors. This maps to the underlying OpenStack/Nova server group policy and is immutable after creation.

publicCloud.instanceGroup.PolicyEnum.description: Instance group placement policy. Scheduling policy that governs how the members of an instance group are placed relative to one another on the underlying hypervisors. `AFFINITY`: Group members are placed onto the same hypervisor host, keeping them physically close together. `ANTI_AFFINITY`: Group members are forced onto different hypervisor hosts, spreading them apart for higher availability.

publicCloud.instanceReservation.Instance.description: A Public Cloud instance reservation: a commitment to a given quantity of instances of a flavor, in a region, for a fixed duration. Once ready, the reservation exposes a dedicated reserved flavor (see currentState.flavor) that instances can be created with to consume the reserved capacity. The object follows the standard envelope: targetSpec is the desired specification supplied by the user, while currentState reflects what the backend actually provisioned.

checksum.description: Checksum. Computed hash of the current target specification, used for optimistic concurrency control.

createdAt.description: Creation date. Timestamp at which the instance reservation was created, in RFC 3339 format.

currentState.description: Current state. Actual state of the instance reservation as reported by the backend, including the reserved flavor to use when creating instances. May be null while the reservation is still being provisioned.

currentTasks.description: Current tasks. Asynchronous operations currently running against this instance reservation. Empty or null when no operation is in progress.

id.description: Unique identifier of the instance reservation

resourceStatus.description: Resource status. Lifecycle status of the instance reservation in the system, for example whether it is being created, ready, or being deleted.

targetSpec.description: Target specification. Desired specification of the instance reservation as supplied by the user (name, location, flavor, quantity and duration). Compare it against currentState to see what the backend actually provisioned.

updatedAt.description: Last update date. Timestamp of the last update of the instance reservation, in RFC 3339 format.

publicCloud.instanceReservation.Instance.description: Instance reservation creation payload. Request body for creating a Public Cloud instance reservation (POST).

targetSpec.description: Target specification. Desired specification of the instance reservation to create.

publicCloud.instanceReservation.Instance.description: Instance reservation current state. Actual state of an instance reservation as observed from the backend.

duration.description: Commitment period of the reservation, as an ISO 8601 duration, for example P1Y for one year

endTime.description: End time. Date at which the reservation commitment ends (startTime plus duration). Null until the reservation is active.

flavor.description: Dedicated flavor created for this reservation. Use its id when creating instances to consume the reserved capacity.

location.description: Current location. Region, and availability zone in a 3-AZ region, where the capacity is reserved.

name.description: Current display name of the instance reservation

orderId.description: Identifier of the order linked to the instance reservation. Null until order is created during reservation creation process.

quantity.description: Quantity. Number of instances of the flavor reserved.

startTime.description: Start time. Date at which the reservation commitment starts. Null until the reservation is active.

publicCloud.instanceReservation.Instance.description: Desired instance reservation specification. User-controlled specification of an instance reservation: what flavor to reserve, how many instances, where and for how long.

duration.description: Commitment period of the reservation, as an ISO 8601 duration, for example P1Y for one year

flavor.description: Reference to the flavor to reserve capacity for

location.description: Target location. Region and, in a 3-AZ region, availability zone where the capacity is reserved. In a 3-AZ region the availability zone is optional: when omitted, the zone with the most stock for the flavor is chosen and returned here. In a region that is not 3-AZ the availability zone is ignored and the reservation is regional. Instances consuming the reservation must be created in this same location.

name.description: Desired display name of the instance reservation

quantity.description: Quantity. Number of instances of the flavor to reserve.

The frontend network the load balancer virtual IP port lives in, as reported by the backend, together with every address through which the VIP is reachable. publicCloud.loadbalancer.LoadbalancerNet.description: Load balancer VIP network address type. Nature of an IP address observed on the load balancer virtual IP port, telling how the address reaches the VIP. `FIXED`: The address configured on the VIP port itself, whether assigned by IPAM or pinned at creation. `FLOATING`: A floating IP associated with the VIP port: the address is not configured on the port, the network translates it to the port fixed address.

Load balancer VIP network reference (desired). User-controlled declaration of the load balancer frontend network: the private network and subnet the virtual IP (VIP) port is created in, and therefore the network the listeners are reachable from. subnetId is mandatory. id is optional: when omitted, the network of the subnet is used, and when given, the subnet must belong to it. The optional IP refines how the VIP is addressed: * omitted. The fixed VIP address is assigned by IPAM inside the subnet. * an address inside the subnet CIDR. Pins the fixed VIP address to that value. * an address outside the subnet CIDR. Designates an EXISTING floating IP to associate with the VIP port. No address is ever allocated on your behalf. The VIP network is set at creation and is IMMUTABLE afterward: it is not part of the update target spec, and neither the network, the subnet, nor the IP can be changed on a load balancer that already exists.

id.description: Identifier of the private network the VIP port is created in. This is the load balancer frontend network, from which its listeners are reachable. When omitted, the network of subnetId is used. Immutable after creation.

ip.description: Address of the virtual IP, whose meaning depends on where it falls relative to the subnet CIDR. Inside the subnet CIDR: pins the fixed VIP address instead of letting IPAM assign it. The address must lie in the subnet allocation pool, must not be the subnet gateway address, and must not already be held by another port. Outside the subnet CIDR: designates an EXISTING floating IP of the project to associate with the VIP port. The floating IP is never created for you, must not already be associated with another port, and the subnet must be attached to a router with an external gateway. A public address requires the optional loadbalancer/usePublicIP IAM action. When omitted, the fixed VIP address is assigned by IPAM. Immutable after creation.

subnetId.description: Identifier of the subnet the VIP port draws its fixed address from. When id is given, the subnet must belong to that network. Immutable after creation.

How users log in to the Harbor web interface and API of the registry. `IAM`: Users log in with OVHcloud accounts, authorized through OVHcloud IAM policies. `LOCAL`: Users log in with accounts created in Harbor. `OIDC`: Users log in through an external OpenID Connect provider. Requires `oidc`.

publicCloud.managedRegistry.AuthorizedIp.description: Authorized IP rule. CIDR block allowed on one or more scopes of the registry.

cidr.description: CIDR. nIPv4 block allowed, for example `192.0.2.0/24`. Mutable.

description.description: Description. Free text describing the rule, for example `VPN`. Null when not set. Mutable.

scopes.description: Scopes. Parts of the registry the CIDR block is allowed on. Mutable.

publicCloud.managedRegistry.AuthorizedIp.description: Authorized IP rule scope. Part of the registry an authorized IP rule applies to. `ADMINISTRATION`: Harbor web interface and management API. `ARTIFACT_OPERATIONS`: Registry endpoint used to push and pull artifacts, for example with `docker` or `helm`.
Authorized IPs. IP filtering of the registry. When `rules` is empty or null, any IP is allowed on every scope. Otherwise a scope accepts only the CIDR blocks of the rules that list it.

rules.description: Rules. CIDR blocks allowed to reach the registry, each on one or more scopes. When empty or null, any IP is allowed. The list is replaced as a whole on update. See AuthorizedIpRule.

publicCloud.managedRegistry.Credentials.description: Administrator credentials. Username and password of the Harbor administrator account of the registry.

password.description: New password of the administrator account. The previous password stops working. Returned by the reset call only.

publicCloud.managedRegistry.Oidc.description: OpenID Connect configuration. External OpenID Connect provider configured as the Harbor login method. Used when `authentication.type` is `OIDC`. Register `<currentState.url>/c/oidc/callback` as a redirect URI of the client in the provider. Each field maps a Harbor OIDC setting, described in the [Harbor documentation](https://goharbor.io/docs/latest/administration/configure-authentication/oidc-auth/).

adminGroup.description: Admin group. Group of the OIDC provider whose members get the Harbor system administrator role. When null, no group gets the role. Requires `groupsClaim`. Mutable.

autoOnboard.description: Automatic onboarding. When `true`, a user logging in for the first time is created from the token claims, without the Harbor onboarding screen. When null, treated as `false`. Mutable.

clientId.description: Client ID. Client identifier of the registry in the OIDC provider. Mutable.

clientSecret.description: Client secret of the registry in the OIDC provider. Required at creation. On update, omit it to keep the current secret, or set it to replace it. Mutable. Write-only: never returned on read.

endpoint.description: Endpoint. Issuer URL of the OIDC provider, for example `https://keycloak.example.com/realms/mpr`. Its `/.well-known/openid-configuration` document must be reachable from the registry. Mutable.

groupFilter.description: Group filter. Regular expression selecting the groups of `groupsClaim` that are imported into Harbor. It does not restrict who can log in. When null, every group is imported. Mutable.

groupsClaim.description: Name of the token claim that lists the groups of the user. When null, groups are not read from the token. Mutable.

name.description: Name of the OIDC provider, displayed on the Harbor login button. Mutable.

scope.description: Comma-separated OIDC scopes requested at login, for example `openid,profile,email,offline_access`. Must include `openid`. Include `offline_access` so the registry gets a refresh token. Mutable.

userClaim.description: Name of the ID token claim used as the Harbor username. The claim must be present in the ID token, otherwise onboarding the user fails. When null, Harbor uses the `name` claim. Mutable.

verifyCert.description: Verify certificate. When `true`, the TLS certificate of `endpoint` is verified. When null, treated as `true`. Set it to `false` only for a provider with a self-signed or untrusted certificate. Mutable.

publicCloud.reference.ProductAvailabilit.description: Possible values for the kind of a product availability link relative to its object
Describes the availability of a model in a single location: whether the region is activated on the project, stock and quota headroom. Read-only reference data.

availabilityZones.description: The availability zones within the location, for example eu-west-par-a, eu-west-par-b, eu-west-par-c. Empty for single-AZ regions.

links.description: Related operations on the location. When quotaStatus is INSUFFICIENT: a QUOTA link to read the quota of the location. Empty otherwise.

name.description: Location name. The region or location identifier, for example GRA11. Identifies the location within a model availability entry.

quotaLimitedBy.description: Quota limited by. The quota resources without enough room, when quotaStatus is INSUFFICIENT. Empty otherwise.

quotaStatus.description: Quota status. Whether the project's quota in the location leaves room for one more unit of the model: one instance with its vCPUs and RAM, one volume, volume snapshot or volume backup of 1 GB, one load balancer, gateway or floating IP, one file storage share of the share type's minimum size, one file storage snapshot. SUFFICIENT or INSUFFICIENT is read from the last quota usage snapshot, which can lag a few minutes behind. SUFFICIENT as well for a product with no tracked quota (public IP, instance snapshot, object storage, Swift) in a region activated on the project. UNKNOWN when the region is not activated on the project or no quota usage is known for it.

regionActivated.description: Whether the region is already activated on the project. When false, the model is sold in the location but the region must be activated on the project before use. This says nothing about stock or quota.

stockStatus.description: The current stock status of the model in the location, keyed by availability-zone name, for example eu-west-par-a. A 3AZ region has one entry per AZ. single-AZ and localzone regions have a single entry. Present only for the instance product type. Absent for every other product type.

publicCloud.reference.ProductAvailabilit.description: Product model availability (read-only reference data). Describes a single offering of a product type and the locations where it is available for the project. Read-only reference data.

links.description: Related operations on the model. A SPECS link points to the reference route listing the technical specifications of the product type: the instance flavor route filtered on the model name, the volume type route, the load balancer flavor route, the gateway model route filtered on the model name, the file storage share type route, or the object storage route. Empty for products without specifications (IPs, snapshots, backups, Swift).

locations.description: The locations where this model is available for the project, each with its activation state. Null or empty when the model is available in no location.

name.description: The offering name within its product type, to use when creating it: the flavor name for an instance (b3-8, win-b3-8) or a load balancer (SMALL to XL), the volume type for a volume (CLASSIC, HIGH_SPEED, HIGH_SPEED_GEN2), the model for a gateway (S to 3XL), the share type for file storage (STANDARD_1AZ), the storage class for object storage (STANDARD, STANDARD_IA, HIGH_PERF, GLACIER_IR, DEEP_ARCHIVE). Products sold as a single model (floating IP, public IP, snapshots, backups, Swift) use their product type as model name.

publicCloud.reference.instance.Flavor.description: Instance flavor (catalog entry). A single compute flavor as advertised by the backend (OpenStack/Nova) for a given region. This is read-only reference data served under /reference: it describes a hardware sizing (vCPUs, RAM, disks) the project can create instances from, not an existing resource. The catalog is per-region. A flavor returned for one region is not guaranteed to exist, or to carry the same characteristics, in another (see location).

bandwidth.description: Network bandwidth an instance of the flavor gets in Mbit/s

description.description: Free-form description of the flavor as reported by the backend. Null when no description is advertised for this flavor.

disk.description: Size of the flavor's root disk in GB. This is the primary system disk provisioned for instances created from this flavor.

ephemeral.description: Size of the flavor's ephemeral disk in GB. Ephemeral storage is transient. Its contents do not survive a rebuild or deletion of the instance. Zero when the flavor provides no ephemeral disk.

gpus.description: Number of physical GPUs provided by the flavor. Zero for flavors without GPU.

id.description: Identifier. The OpenStack/Nova flavor ID. Stable within a region and used to reference the flavor when creating an instance.

isPublic.description: Public availability. Whether the flavor is publicly available to the project. Private flavors are only visible to the projects they have been explicitly shared with.

location.description: Location. Region where this flavor is offered. The flavor catalog is per-region: a flavor returned for one region is not guaranteed to exist, or to carry the same characteristics, in another. regionActivated tells whether the region is already activated on the project. When false, the region must be activated on the project before use. availabilityZones lists the availability zones of the region, empty for a single-AZ region.

name.description: The backend flavor name, for example b2-7, c2-15. This is the commercial/technical name used to identify the sizing in the catalog.

ram.description: RAM in MB. Amount of memory provided by the flavor, expressed in MB.

This is read-only reference data served under /reference: it describes a bootable image the project can create instances from, not an existing resource. The image catalog is read-only in APIv2. There is no create, update or delete on images. The catalog is per-region: an image returned for one region is not guaranteed to exist in another (see location).

When `createFrom` is set, the encryption of the snapshot's source file storage is used and returned here: requesting `enabled` true from a snapshot of an unencrypted file storage is rejected as an invalid parameter, and requesting `enabled` false from a snapshot of an encrypted file storage is ignored, so the new file storage is encrypted.

post.description: Creates an AI agent: a hosted assistant that answers on its own URL, given by `currentState.endpointUrl`, and reached with a token from the `token` action. An agent runs a model with a persona, plus whatever tools, memory and channels its configuration gives it. That configuration can come from a ready-made one published by OVHcloud, from a template of your own, or from settings supplied here — or from none of them, leaving an agent that cannot answer until it is given a model. Parts of it that OVHcloud manages are rejected here; the `globalSettings` preset says which. This is the only point at which this API sets an agent's configuration: from here on the agent holds its own and is configured through its endpoint. Create it paused to finish preparing it before it answers anyone.

Restating the agent's current running state changes nothing; stating the other one pauses or resumes it. `targetSpec.name` is optional: omitting it, or restating the current name, leaves it untouched. Any other name renames the agent and redeploys it, keeping its identifier, its access tokens, its configuration and its data, and re-applying its paused state. A name another agent in the project already holds is rejected. The configuration is not settable here; it is read and changed through the agent itself.

get.description:
### List instances

Lists all instances in the project. Each item is a full instance envelope with the same shape as the `GET` route (desired `targetSpec` and observed `currentState`).

### Filesystem attachments
For performance, `currentState.shares` is not populated in list responses. To see the filesystems attached to a given instance, call `GET .../instance/{instanceId}` on it.

### Filters
The optional `name`, `flavor`, `region` and `status` query parameters narrow the list. Each one can be repeated, for example `?status=READY&status=CREATING`: repeated values of the same parameter are combined with OR, and different parameters are combined with AND. Filters apply only within the instances you are authorized to list. An unknown `status` value or an unavailable `region` is rejected with a `400 InvalidParameter`.

parameters.name: flavor
parameters.description: Filter by flavor ID or flavor name. Repeatable.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Filter by instance name (case-insensitive substring match). Repeatable.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Filter by instance region. An unavailable region is rejected. Repeatable.

post.description:
### Create an instance

Provisions a new instance from the supplied `targetSpec`. Creation is asynchronous: the resource starts in `CREATING` and becomes `READY` once the backend has booted it. Poll `GET .../instance/{instanceId}` until `resourceStatus` is `READY` and `currentTasks` is empty.

### Create-time-only fields (immutable afterward)
Several fields can be set only at creation and can never be changed later:
* `location` — the region (and optional availability zone) the instance is deployed in.
* `sshKeyName` — the SSH key injected into the instance at boot.
* `group` — placement / instance-group membership. It binds the instance to an existing instance group (Nova server group) for `AFFINITY` / `ANTI_AFFINITY` scheduling. Server-group membership is fixed by OpenStack at boot and cannot be added, removed, or changed afterward — there is no group `PUT`.

### User data (cloud-init)
`targetSpec.userData` is a base64-encoded (strict standard encoding) cloud-init payload handed to the instance at boot through the OpenStack metadata service / config drive, and interpreted by cloud-init inside the guest image. The encoded string must be at most 65535 bytes. It is write-only: the value is never returned by `GET`/`LIST`. It is also not persisted or stored by the Public Cloud API: the payload is handed to the compute service, which makes it available to the instance via the metadata service. Only a non-reversible fingerprint of the value is retained, for change detection. Unlike the create-time-only fields above, `userData` can be changed later via `PUT`. See the `PUT` route for the destructive semantics of doing so.

### Declarative `volumes`
`targetSpec.volumes` is a declarative list of block-volume references attached to the instance. Supply the volumes to attach at boot. On a subsequent `PUT` the list is diffed to attach or detach volumes (see the `PUT` route). There is no imperative attach/detach endpoint.

### Declarative `shares`
`targetSpec.shares` is a declarative list of filesystem (Manila share) attachments. Each entry references a share plus an optional per-entry `accessLevel` (defaults to `READ_WRITE`). At creation, each attach creates a Manila IP access rule for the instance's interface on the share's network. The instance must have an interface on that network. As with volumes, the list is reconciled by diffing on `PUT`.

### Declarative `networks` and public IPs
`targetSpec.networks` is a declarative list of network interfaces. Each entry is `{id?, subnetId?, ip?, autoAssignPublicIp?}`, and the fields you set decide what it means:
* `{"autoAssignPublicIp": true}` — a public (Ext-Net) interface with a platform-assigned public IP. At most one entry may set it.
* `{"ip": "..."}` without a network `id` — a public IP the project already owns: either an existing additional IP (also known as a failover IP), or an Ext-Net IP of the project in the instance's region. Any other address is rejected. Such an entry implicitly attaches the public (Ext-Net) interface. Several are allowed, and they may coexist with an `autoAssignPublicIp` entry.
* `{"id": "...", "subnetId": "..."}` — a private interface whose fixed address is assigned by IPAM.
* `{"id": "...", "subnetId": "...", "ip": "..."}` — a private interface where `ip` pins the fixed address when it falls inside the subnet CIDR, and otherwise designates an existing floating IP to associate with that interface (the floating IP must already exist).

Any entry that sets `autoAssignPublicIp` or carries a public `ip` requires the optional `instance/usePublicIP` IAM action, including floating IP associations.

In `currentState.networks` the shape is different: there is one entry per network plus at most one id-less entry for the public (Ext-Net) interface, and every address is reported through that entry's `addresses` list. There is no scalar `ip`. Each address carries a `type`: `FIXED` for an address configured on the interface itself (a private fixed address, whether IPAM-assigned or pinned, and the Ext-Net address), `FLOATING` for a floating IP associated with the interface, and `ADDITIONAL` for an additional IP routed to the public interface (additional IPs no longer form their own entry). `autoAssignPublicIp` is never echoed back, because the backend cannot distinguish a platform-assigned address from a pinned one.

delete.description:
### Delete an instance

Permanently deletes a Public Cloud instance. Deletion is asynchronous: the resource transitions to `DELETING`, the response echoes the instance, and the backend then removes it. Poll `GET .../instance/{instanceId}` until it returns `InstanceDoesNotExist` (`404`) to confirm removal.

Behavior
* Independent block volumes attached to the instance are detached, not deleted — they are separate resources and survive.
* Filesystem (share) attachments are released as part of the teardown.

A delete already in progress is reported as `ResourceAlreadyBeingDeleted`. An instance in a transient or otherwise invalid state may be rejected with `ResourceInInvalidState`.

get.description:
### Get an instance

Returns a single Public Cloud instance, including its desired `targetSpec` and observed `currentState`.

### Optimistic concurrency
The `checksum` returned here is the hash of the current `targetSpec`. Keep it and send it back on any subsequent `PUT` or imperative `action` call on the instance to guard against lost updates. It is optional, but omitting it forces the write (see the `PUT` route).

### Filesystem attachments
`currentState.shares` — the list of filesystems (Manila shares) attached to the instance — is populated only on this single-instance `GET`. It is deliberately not returned by the `LIST` route for performance reasons. Fetch the individual instance when you need it.

put.description:
### Update an instance

This is the single, declarative route for changing an instance. You do not call verb-specific endpoints. Instead you submit a new desired `targetSpec` and the API derives the operations to perform from the diff against the current specification. (Imperative power/lifecycle operations such as reboot, start, stop, and rescue live on the separate `.../instance/{instanceId}/action` route.)

### Asynchronous, desired-state model
1. You send the new `targetSpec`, optionally together with the `checksum` from your last `GET`.
2. If accepted, you immediately get back the instance with the updated `targetSpec` and a new `checksum`. `resourceStatus` becomes `UPDATING`.
3. One or more asynchronous tasks reconcile `currentState` toward `targetSpec`. Poll `GET .../instance/{instanceId}` until `resourceStatus` is `READY` and `currentTasks` is empty to know the change has been applied.

### Operations derived from the diff
* Rename — changing `name` renames the instance.
* Resize (flavor) — changing `flavor` migrates the instance to the new flavor.
* Volume attach / detach — done declaratively by diffing the `volumes` list: adding a volume reference attaches that volume, removing one detaches it. There is no imperative attach/detach endpoint — the diff is the only mechanism.
* Network attach / detach — done declaratively by diffing the `networks` list, whose entries are `{id?, subnetId?, ip?, autoAssignPublicIp?}`: a platform-assigned Ext-Net IP (`{"autoAssignPublicIp": true}`, at most one entry), a public IP the project already owns — additional IP or project Ext-Net IP in the instance's region — (`{"ip"}`, no network `id`), a private interface with an IPAM address (`{"id", "subnetId"}`), or a private interface with `ip` either pinning its fixed address (address inside the subnet CIDR) or associating an existing floating IP (address outside it). Any entry that sets `autoAssignPublicIp` or carries a public `ip` requires the optional `instance/usePublicIP` IAM action.
* Filesystem (share) attach / detach — done declaratively by diffing the `shares` list. Adding an entry attaches the share: it creates a Manila IP access rule for the instance's interface on the share's network, so the instance must already have an interface on that network or the attach errors. Removing an entry detaches the share: the matching access rule is removed, and the detach is idempotent. Each entry's `accessLevel` defaults to `READ_WRITE`. Caveat: managing per-share access rules directly on the share resource *and* attaching the same share instance-side here is unsupported — the share will report `OUT_OF_SYNC`.

### Immutable fields (excluded from update)
`location`, `sshKeyName`, and `group` are set only at creation and are not part of the update. In particular, placement-group (`group`) membership cannot change post-create. OpenStack/Nova server groups are immutable and there is deliberately no group `PUT`.

### Destructive update (`userData`)
Changing `targetSpec.userData` reinstalls the instance — a Nova rebuild on its current image — which wipes the root disk and all data on it. Semantics are tri-state: omitting the field (or sending `null`) keeps the current value unchanged, an empty string `""` clears it, and any other value replaces it. Both the clear and the replace trigger the reinstall. An instance with no `image` (boot-from-volume) has nothing to rebuild onto, so a `userData` change on it is rejected with a `400 InvalidParameter`.

### Optimistic concurrency (`checksum`)
The `checksum` guards against lost updates and is optional. When you send it, it must match the server-side value: if another request modified the instance since your last `GET`, the checksum no longer matches and the request is rejected with a checksum-mismatch error (`ChecksumMismatch`). Re-`GET` the instance and retry against the fresh state. When you omit it (or send an empty string), the check is skipped and the update is forced (last-write-wins).

post.description:
### Perform an instance action

Imperative endpoint for power and lifecycle actions on an instance. This is the one place such imperative operations live. Distinct from the declarative `PUT` on the instance, which reconciles desired state from a `targetSpec` diff. Actions are asynchronous: the instance transitions through the relevant transient state and the response echoes the instance. Poll `GET .../instance/{instanceId}` until `resourceStatus` is `READY` and `currentTasks` is empty.

### Action `type`
The `type` field selects the operation:
* `REBOOT` — reboot the instance (`parameters.hard` chooses a hard vs. soft reboot).
* `START` / `STOP` — power the instance on / off.
* `SHELVE` / `UNSHELVE` — shelve the instance (freeing hypervisor resources) and restore it.
* `PAUSE` / `UNPAUSE` — freeze a running instance in the memory of the host, and unfreeze it.
* `SUSPEND` / `RESUME` — save the memory state of a running instance to disk and stop it, and restore it.
* `RESCUE` / `UNRESCUE` — boot into rescue mode (optionally from `parameters.imageId`) and return to normal boot.
* `LOCK` / `UNLOCK` — lock the instance against accidental actions / modifications, and unlock it.

### Optimistic concurrency (`checksum`)
The `checksum` is optional. When you send it, it must match the current server-side value or the action is rejected with a checksum-mismatch error. Re-`GET` and retry. When you omit it (or send an empty string), the check is skipped and the action is forced (last-write-wins). An action requested while the instance is in an incompatible state is rejected with `ResourceInInvalidState`.

Reboot instance.summary: Perform a hard reboot on an instance

Rescue instance.summary: Put an instance in rescue mode

get.description:
### Compatible flavors

Returns the list of flavors this instance can be resized to. The list is computed from the instance's current flavor and the catalog of flavors available in the instance's region.

The following rules apply to the returned list:

- It excludes the instance's current flavor.
- It includes only flavors whose disk size is greater than or equal to the current flavor's disk size (a resize cannot shrink the root disk).
- It includes only flavors in the same region as the instance.
- It includes only flavors whose plan is available in the instance's region.
- It is empty for baremetal instances, which cannot be resized.

Each item has the same shape as an entry from the flavor reference catalog (`publicCloud.reference.instance.Flavor`). Its `location.regionActivated` is true, since the instance's region is activated on the project. `location.availabilityZones` lists the availability zones of the region, for example eu-west-par-a, eu-west-par-b and eu-west-par-c, and is empty for a single-AZ region.
