### Create a remote console

Opens a remote console session to the instance and returns the connection details (a `url` and, depending on the protocol, an access `token`) for a client to connect. This is a synchronous call — no desired-state reconciliation — and the returned URL is short-lived, so request a fresh console when it expires.

### Protocol and type
Choose the console via the request body:
* `protocol` — the console transport, for example `VNC`, `SPICE`, `SERIAL`.
* `type` — the concrete console kind for that protocol, for example `NOVNC` for `VNC`, `SERIAL` for `SERIAL`.

The instance must be in a state that supports a console, otherwise the request is rejected with `ResourceInInvalidState`.

### List instance groups

Lists all instance groups (placement groups) in the project, each with the same shape as the `GET` route (scheduling `policy` and members).

### Immutable by design
Instance groups cannot be modified after creation. There is deliberately no `PUT` / update route, and membership is fixed at *instance* creation time via the instance's `targetSpec.group` field. See the `GET` route for details.

post.description:
### Create an instance group

Creates a new instance group (placement group). Creation is asynchronous: the group starts in `CREATING` and becomes `READY` once the backend has provisioned it.

### Placement policy
`targetSpec.policy` chooses how members are scheduled relative to each other:
* `AFFINITY` — members are placed on the same hypervisor.
* `ANTI_AFFINITY` — members are placed on different hypervisors (for high availability).

### Immutable, membership set at instance creation
The group is immutable once created. There is deliberately no `PUT` / update route, so the `policy` can never be changed. The group is created empty: instances are not added here. An instance joins the group only at its own creation time, via its `targetSpec.group` field (see the instance `POST`), and membership cannot change afterward (OpenStack/Nova server groups are immutable).

### Delete an instance group

Deletes an instance group (placement group). Deletion is asynchronous: the resource transitions to `DELETING` and the backend then removes it.

A group is normally removed once it is empty (has no member instances). Because membership is fixed at *instance* creation time and cannot be edited on an existing group, freeing a group means deleting or recreating its member instances first. Deleting the group tears down only the placement grouping. It does not delete the instances themselves. A delete already in progress is reported as `ResourceAlreadyBeingDeleted`.

To change grouping you delete and recreate the affected instances into a different group.

The body carries the complete desired state of every field `publicCloud.publicIp.FloatingIPUpdateTargetSpec` exposes, which today is `description` alone. `description` is optional: restate it to keep it, and leave it out to clear it. The create-only field `location` cannot be changed once the floating IP exists. It is deliberately absent from the update model, and sending it is rejected with a 400.

### Product availability

Returns the products available to this Public Cloud project, grouped by product type.

This is read-only reference data: the response is computed from the OVHcloud commercial catalog combined with the project's entitlements and its quota usage. It does not reflect existing resources and triggers no OpenStack call.

The response is an array with one entry per product type, in this order: `INSTANCE`, `VOLUME`, `LOADBALANCER`, `GATEWAY`, `FLOATING_IP`, `PUBLIC_IP`, `VOLUME_SNAPSHOT`, `VOLUME_BACKUP`, `INSTANCE_SNAPSHOT`, `SHARE`, `SHARE_SNAPSHOT`, `OBJECT_STORAGE`, `SWIFT`. Each type group carries its `models`. Each model carries the `locations` where it is sold to the project, in the regions activated on the project and in those the project can activate. Each location reports its availability zones, `regionActivated`, a `quotaStatus` with the quota resources that block it (`quotaLimitedBy`) and, for the `INSTANCE` type only, a `stockStatus` per availability zone.

`links` point to related operations: a `SPECS` link on a model leads to the reference route describing it, and a location whose `quotaStatus` is `INSUFFICIENT` carries a `QUOTA` link.

Every filter is optional: `type` keeps the group of that product type only, `region` the locations of that region (letter case ignored), `name` the models with exactly that name and `nameContains` the models whose name contains that value (letter case ignored).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Optional exact model name filter, for example b3-8

parameters.name: nameContains
parameters.description: Optional model name filter keeping the names that contain this value, letter case ignored

The body carries the complete desired state of every field `publicCloud.blockStorage.BlockUpdateTargetSpec` exposes (`name`, `size` and `volumeType`), so read the volume first and restate every value you want to keep: a field left out of `targetSpec` is cleared, not carried over from the stored specification.

The create-only fields `location`, `encryption` and `createFrom` cannot be changed once the volume exists. They are deliberately absent from the update model, and sending one is rejected with a 400.

`name` and `size` are both required. `size` can only grow: restate the volume's current size to keep it, or send a larger value to extend it, because shrinking a volume is not supported. Leaving `size` out, or sending 0, is rejected with a 400. Restate `volumeType` to keep it. Sending a different type triggers an online retype (migration).

The optional `checksum` guards against a lost update: when supplied it must match the volume's current checksum or the request is rejected with a 409 checksum mismatch. Omitting it skips the check and forces the write (last-write-wins).
